The Olympic victor, I said, is thought happy when he receives only a part of the blessedness that is secured for our citizens. Their victory is more glorious, and their maintenance at public cost is more complete. The victory they have won is the salvation of the whole State. The crown they and their children wear is everything that life needs. They receive rewards from their country while they live, and after death an honorable burial.

Then, since the case is decided, I demand on behalf of justice that the esteem in which gods and men hold her, and which we acknowledge to be her due, should now be restored to her by us. She has been shown to confer reality and not to deceive those who truly possess her. So let what has been taken from her be given back, so that she may also win the prize of appearance, which is hers too, and which she gives to her own.
